newsitem.title: USA: Integrated Health sees no Medicare problem.
newsitem.headline: Integrated Health sees no Medicare problem.

text.p: Integrated Health Services Inc said on Friday it was not having material or significant problems with Medicare reimbursements and would not need to revise its earnings.
On Thursday, competitor Mariner Health Group Inc said it would take a one-time charge of $10 million in the third quarter to increase reserves covering changes in Medicare reimbursements.
Integrated said it had not experienced any dramatic new trends in the last to six to 12 months and would not need to adjust or reduce anticipated Medicare reimbursements.
"Integrated Health Service believes that an individual company may be experiencing a problem because of its particular Medicare fiscal intermediary," the company said.
First Call puts the company's third quarter earnings at $0.56 per share.
"We're comfortable with the street estimates," said Integrated Chief Executive Robert Elkins, adding that the company will report its results around October 31.
Integrated said in operating a health care company there were always individual issues and disputes with Medicare.
